answer: Blind-signed hardware attestation resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to mint one blind token per TPM endorsement key at the dawn of an epoch. Issuers log a hardware nullifier to block duplicate issuance, keeping clones from creeping like a vine across the agent orchard, while peers verify only the blind signature. Attackers incur the verifiable cost of acquiring separate physical chips per identity. However, leaked vendor keys or device farms can still yield excess accounts.
